name: James Bond (Card Game)
description: James Bond is a high-speed, frantic card game that tests memory and reaction time. Unlike turn-based games, everyone plays simultaneously. Each player manages several 'books' (piles) of cards, racing to turn each book into a set of four-of-a-kind by swapping cards with a shared central pool. The first player to complete all their sets and shout 'James Bond!' wins.

content.text: James Bond is a high-speed, frantic card game that tests memory and reaction time. Unlike turn-based games, everyone plays simultaneously. Each player manages several 'books' (piles) of cards, racing to turn each book into a set of four-of-a-kind by swapping cards with a shared central pool. The first player to complete all their sets and shout 'James Bond!' wins.
A variation of children's 'Speed' and 'Spoons' games. The name likely comes from the '007' high-stakes imagery and the intense, rapid pace of the game.

- 2 players: 24 cards each (6 books of 4).
- 3 players: 16 cards each (4 books of 4).
- 4 players: 12 cards each (3 books of 4).
Deal all cards into piles of 4, leaving exactly 4 cards face-up in the center (the 'Pond').

items.text: Book announcement: Some players say 'book' each time they complete a pile of four equal cards, and 'book, James Bond' when they complete the last pile. Saying 'book' is not required and may give away information.
Win-call name: The word used to claim a win varies by region: James Bond, Chanhassen, Atlantis, or the name of the game in other versions.
Multi-card trade: Some groups allow more than one card to be traded simultaneously (e.g. grab both fours at once in exchange for two cards from the pile).
